title: Elon Musk Pledges SpaceX Share to Every U.S. Child Next Year
dek: The billionaire's announcement follows Anthropic's Public Benefit Fund pledge and could distribute over $10 billion in SpaceX stock to roughly 73 million children.
metaDescription: Elon Musk announced on X he will give one SpaceX share to every child in America next year, a potential giveaway valued at over $10 billion based on current…

sections.heading: Musk Announces SpaceX Share Giveaway on X
sections.body: Elon Musk posted on X on Monday stating he will give one SpaceX share to every child in America next year, adding "This will be the first of many" in the same post [1][2][3]. The announcement came in response to Anthropic's Sunday announcement of a Public Benefit Fund committing at least 5% of its shares [1][2]. Musk replied to Anthropic's post on X recommending giving shares directly to the public and stating that is what he will do [1][2]. SpaceX shares closed at about $146 on Friday [1][2].

sections.heading: Valuation Estimates and Share Count Discrepancies
sections.body: The potential giveaway value varies across reports based on different child population figures and share price calculations. CNBC cites U.S. Census Bureau data from July 1, 2025, showing 72 million children under 18, calculating a giveaway worth about $10.5 billion at the $146.03 closing price [1]. CNN estimates roughly 73 million people under 18 in the U.S., valuing the giveaway at about $10.7 billion [2]. Yahoo Finance also cites approximately 73 million children but does not provide a dollar valuation [3]. Yahoo Finance further breaks down the Census data, noting about 18.5 million children aged newborn up to 4 years old in America [3].

sections.heading: Musk's SpaceX Holdings and Recent Market Activity
sections.body: According to CNBC citing an August SEC filing, Musk currently owns about 4.8 billion SpaceX shares, rising to 6.4 billion with unvested awards and options, representing a 48.4% beneficial stake [1]. This specific ownership data appears only in CNBC's reporting. Yahoo Finance reports SpaceX stock rose 1% in premarket trading on Monday following the announcement [3]. CNN notes SpaceX only began trading publicly in June and had the biggest initial public offering in history [2], a claim not mentioned by the other outlets.

sections.heading: Related Developments: Anthropic Fund and Trump Accounts
sections.body: Anthropic's Public Benefit Fund commits at least 5% of its shares, which CNN values at $48 billion at the private company's latest valuation [2]. CNN also reports Anthropic recently warned of the "existential risk to humanity" posed by AI technology [2]. Separately, CNN references a Treasury Department program automatically signing up millions of under-18s to "Trump Accounts" with a one-off $1,000 government contribution for children born 2025-2028 [2]. Yahoo Finance adds that SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell pledged a personal donation of over $320 million in SpaceX stock to fund Trump Accounts for more than two million children [3]. CNN also mentions new movies "The Social Reckoning" and documentary "You Can See Everything" as reminders of Big Tech recklessness [2].

keyTakeaways: Elon Musk announced on X he will give one SpaceX share to every U.S. child next year, calling it the first of many such giveaways.
The giveaway could be worth $10.5-10.7 billion based on ~72-73 million children and a ~$146 share price.
Musk's announcement directly responded to Anthropic's pledge of 5% of shares to a Public Benefit Fund.
SpaceX shares rose 1% in premarket trading Monday after the announcement.
Related developments include Gwynne Shotwell's $320M+ SpaceX stock pledge to Trump Accounts and Anthropic's $48B fund valuation.
whyItMatters: Musk's pledge represents an unprecedented direct wealth transfer to children via equity in a major private space company, potentially creating a generation of retail shareholders. The move frames corporate philanthropy as direct ownership distribution rather than foundation-based giving, responding to Anthropic's similar but fund-structured approach.
